title: Distributed Tracing (OpenTelemetry)
summary: Connect agent decisions, retrieval, model calls, and tool effects into one causal execution record using interoperable trace context.
overview: Distributed tracing represents a request as timed operations called spans, connected by parent relationships or explicit links. For agents, the important unit is not merely the HTTP call: planning iterations, queued jobs, retrieval, inference, validation, and external effects each contribute to the outcome. OpenTelemetry supplies instrumentation and export conventions while the application defines meaningful workflow boundaries.

Trace context should follow work across HTTP, messaging, and asynchronous execution. A retry needs its own attempt span under the same logical operation; a batch assembled from several requests can use span links. Trace data is operational evidence, not a license to store full prompts, credentials, customer documents, or private reasoning.

production.poc: A prototype traces one successful turn and verifies that model and tool timing explain its total duration.
production.production: Production propagates context through queues, correlates logs, redacts attributes, and defines error classification and sampling.
production.scale: Enterprise scale needs collector capacity, stable semantic naming, controlled cardinality, cross-team ownership, and sampling strategies that retain unusual failures without collecting every payload.

components.name: Instrumentation SDK
components.role: Creates spans around workflow stages and injects or extracts context at boundaries.

components.name: Context carrier
components.role: Transfers trace identifiers through request headers or message metadata.

components.name: Collector
components.role: Receives, filters, batches, and exports telemetry without coupling the agent to one backend.

components.name: Trace backend
components.role: Stores causal execution records and enables latency and error investigation.

components.name: Redaction policy
components.role: Allow-lists attributes and protects sensitive prompt or tool data before export.

flow.title: Start logical request
flow.description: Create a root span carrying a stable task type, tenant classification, and workflow revision without raw personal data.

flow.title: Propagate execution context
flow.description: Inject context when calling tools or publishing work; extract it in the receiving process.

flow.title: Create semantic child spans
flow.description: Separate retrieval, provider queueing, inference, validation, and side-effect commit timings.

flow.title: Record attempt outcomes
flow.description: Attach model revision, token usage, retry reason, and structured error category to the appropriate attempt.

flow.title: Export safely
flow.description: Batch telemetry through a collector with bounded buffers and backpressure behavior that cannot block business work indefinitely.

flow.title: Investigate causal paths
flow.description: Correlate a failed workflow with logs and metrics while distinguishing parallel work from critical-path latency.

diagrams.title: A queued agent trace
diagrams.code:
sequenceDiagram
 participant G as Gateway
 participant A as Agent
 participant Q as Work queue
 participant W as Tool worker
 participant C as Collector
 G->>A: Request with trace context
 A->>Q: Task and context carrier
 Q->>W: Deliver work
 W->>W: Tool attempt span
 W-->>A: Result and operation identifier
 A-->>G: Validated answer
 A-->>C: Agent spans
 W-->>C: Linked worker spans
diagrams.caption: Queue transport must preserve causal context even when the producing request has already returned.

useCase.title: Finding the slow step in a maintenance agent
useCase.situation: A plant assistant reads equipment alarms, retrieves manuals, and asks a maintenance API for recent work orders.
useCase.problem: Operators report occasional slow answers, but aggregate model latency appears normal.
useCase.requirement: Locate the causal bottleneck without exporting proprietary manuals or machine credentials.
useCase.architecture: Instrumentation wraps retrieval and work-order calls, propagates context through a job queue, and exports only approved identifiers.
runtime: A slow interaction produces separate queue, retrieval, and inference spans.
The trace reveals repeated work-order timeouts before the model starts generating.
useCase.failure: If the collector becomes unavailable, bounded local buffering drops telemetry according to policy while the assistant continues serving.
useCase.impact: Track trace completeness, critical-path time, and dropped telemetry; the value is actionable diagnosis rather than a larger collection of disconnected logs.

tradeoffs.benefit: Reveal hidden queueing and retry costs.
Can retain traces with observed failures or unusual latency.
tradeoffs.cost: Requires buffering and more collector resources.
May require protected application records for deeper reproduction.

failures.detection: Worker spans appear as unrelated roots.
failures.recovery: Test context serialization and use links where parentage is inappropriate.

failures.detection: Index size and query latency grow with unique raw values.
failures.recovery: Replace uncontrolled labels with bounded categories or non-indexed approved identifiers.

mistakes.fix: Use an attribute allow-list and separate governed evidence storage.

mistakes.mistake: Treating retries as one opaque span
mistakes.fix: Record each attempt and its reason under a logical operation.
Use bounded asynchronous export with explicit loss metrics.

whenToUse: Use for workflows crossing services or asynchronous queues.
Use when latency and cost cannot be explained by provider metrics alone.
Use to correlate tool effects with the agent request that caused them.
whenNotToUse: Do not treat traces as an authoritative transaction ledger.
Avoid storing secrets or unrestricted model payloads in span attributes.
Avoid tracing every token as an individual span at high throughput.
checklist: Measure collector drops and queue depth.
Verify one complete failure trace end to end.
